recipes.title: Ashoka Halwa
recipes.description: Rich Thiruvaiyaru wedding halwa of roasted moong dal and wheat flour cooked down with sugar and ghee.

ingredients.name: red food colouring, mixed in 1 tsp water

steps.instructionText: Dry roast the moong dal until it smells nutty and browns slightly.
Add the water and pressure cook for 7-8 whistles, until the dal is soft and mushy.
Heat 4 tbsp of the ghee in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-low heat and cook the wheat flour in it until golden brown.
Stir the cooked dal into the flour and let it thicken for 5 minutes, then add the sugar.
Stirring continuously, add 6-7 tbsp more ghee, 1 tbsp at a time, for 12-15 minutes, until the mixture leaves the sides of the pan as a dough.
Heat the last 1 tbsp of ghee in a small pan and fry the cashews until slightly brown. Add them to the halwa.
Mix in the cardamom powder and the red food colouring.
Take the pan off the heat and let the halwa cool.

recipes.title: Bihari Kabab
recipes.description: Pakistani-style kababs of meat marinated in roasted whole spices, yogurt and lemon, then grilled on skewers.

ingredients.name: mutton, lamb or beef, cut into small pieces

steps.instructionText: Dry roast the cumin seeds, coriander seeds, fennel seeds and mustard seeds in a small pan over medium heat until fragrant.
Grind the roasted spices in a spice grinder or with a mortar and pestle.
Mix the ground spices with the ginger paste, garlic paste, garam masala, paprika, chilli flakes, turmeric, salt, yogurt, lemon juice and oil.
Put the mutton in a large bowl, pour over the marinade and mix to coat. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Heat a grill to medium-high. Thread the mutton onto skewers and grill for 8-10 minutes, turning occasionally, until cooked through (or bake at 200 °C / 400 °F for 15-20 minutes).
Serve the kababs hot with rice or naan.

recipes.title: Bhel Puri
recipes.description: Mumbai beach snack of puffed rice, sev, potato and onion tossed with green and sweet date-tamarind chutneys.

steps.instructionText: For the spicy chutney, grind half the coriander leaves with the mint leaves, garlic, green chillies and a little salt to a fine paste, adding some water.
For the sweet chutney, grind the date pulp, tamarind pulp, jaggery, 2 tsp of the chilli powder and the cumin seeds to a fine paste with some water.
Mix the puffed rice with most of the sev. Add the chaat masala, salt and the remaining 1 tsp chilli powder.
Add the onion, raw mango, potatoes and most of the remaining coriander leaves, and mix gently with your hands.
Just before serving, mix in the spicy chutney and the sweet chutney.
Put the bhel on plates and top with more sev and chutney. Garnish with the last of the coriander leaves and serve with the puris.

recipes.title: Cucumber Pachadi
recipes.description: Kerala side dish of grated cucumber warmed with a coconut-cumin paste and a mustard seed tempering.

steps.instructionText: Peel the cucumber, cut it in half lengthways and scoop out and discard the seeds.
Grate the cucumber, or cut it into very small pieces.
Cook the cucumber in the microwave for 4-5 minutes.
Meanwhile, grind the grated coconut and cumin seeds to a fine paste.
Heat the oil in a kadai. Add the mustard seeds and red chillies and let them splutter.
Add the cooked cucumber, the coconut paste and salt. Mix well and warm over a low flame; it should not boil.
Take it off the stove as soon as it starts to boil, and serve with rice or roti.

recipes.title: Mysore Pak
recipes.description: Karnataka sweet of roasted besan cooked in sugar syrup with lots of ghee until it sets crisp and porous.

steps.instructionText: Roast the besan in a small amount of the ghee.
Boil the sugar, cardamom powder and a splash of water in a saucepan to a single-thread syrup. If more than one thread forms, add a little more water.
Keeping the heat on, mix half the roasted besan into the hot syrup.
Gradually stir in half the ghee, and keep stirring until the ghee is absorbed.
Repeat with the remaining besan and ghee, adding ghee only until the mixture stops absorbing it.
When the mixture turns crisp and bubbly, pour it into a tray and let it cool.
Cut the Mysore pak into pieces of the shape you like.

recipes.title: Chocolate Sandesh
recipes.description: Quick no-cook Bengali sweet of mashed fresh paneer with cocoa, cream and vanilla, rolled into balls.

steps.instructionText: Mash the paneer and sugar substitute together well.
Add the cream, cocoa powder and vanilla essence and mix well.
Divide the mixture into 8 equal parts and roll each into a ball.
Refrigerate the sandesh for at least 1 hour, then serve.

recipes.title: Coconut Rice
recipes.description: South Indian rice tossed with coconut, chana dal, cashews and curry leaves toasted in a mustard seed tadka.

ingredients.name: grated coconut (fresh, frozen or dry flakes)

steps.instructionText: Heat the oil with the mustard seeds in a covered pan.
When the mustard seeds have stopped popping, add the coconut, red chillies, curry leaves, chana dal, salt and cashews.
Toast everything lightly in the oil until golden.
Add this seasoning to the cooked rice, mix well and serve.

recipes.title: Murukku
recipes.description: Crunchy South Indian spirals of rice flour and roasted urad dal with sesame and cumin, pressed and deep fried.

steps.instructionText: Dry roast the urad dal, grind it to a fine powder and set aside.
In a wide bowl, mix the rice flour, urad dal powder, chilli powder, salt, sesame seeds and cumin seeds. Mix in the hot oil.
Add enough water to make a dough with the consistency of roti dough.
Heat the oil for deep frying in a deep pan.
Press the dough through a murukku mould into the heated oil. Fry in batches until light golden brown.
Drain the murukku on paper towels.

recipes.title: Methi Muthiya
recipes.description: Gujarati fried dumplings of fenugreek leaves, wheat flour and besan, lightly sweet and spiced.

steps.instructionText: Heat the oil for deep frying.
In a bowl, mix the methi leaves, wheat flour, besan, hing, sugar, chilli-ginger paste and the hot oil into a dough.
Divide the dough into 15-20 equal portions and roll each into a round ball.
Fry the balls in batches of 10-12 over a low flame until golden brown.
Drain on absorbent paper and serve.

recipes.title: Dosa
recipes.description: Thin, crisp South Indian crepes made from a fermented batter of rice, urad dal and fenugreek.

steps.instructionText: Soak the rice, urad dal and fenugreek seeds separately: the rice for 6-8 hours, the dal for only 3-4 hours.
Grind the soaked rice, dal and fenugreek seeds together in a blender to a very smooth batter.
Add the salt and enough water for a dropping consistency. Leave to rise for 5-6 hours or overnight.
Check the batter and, if needed, add water to make a smooth pouring consistency.
Heat a tava until very hot and splash a little water over it. Pour on a ladle of batter at once and spread it thin in circles without pressing hard.
Lower the heat and dribble a little oil around the edges. When the edges start to brown, it is almost done.
Flip the dosa and cook the other side for a few seconds. Fold it over, with a filling if you like, and serve.

recipes.title: Masala Dosa
recipes.description: Crisp fermented rice and urad dal crepe spread with onion chutney and folded over spiced potato masala.

ingredients.name: medium potatoes, boiled and coarsely mashed

steps.instructionText: The day before, grind the ponni rice, parboiled rice, urad dal and salt with water in a blender or wet grinder to a batter like pancake batter.
Set the batter aside overnight in a warm spot to ferment. Use a big container, as it can nearly double.
For the filling, heat the oil in a wok, add the mustard seeds and let them splutter.
As the spluttering slows, add the green chillies, curry leaves and chana dal. Stir until the chana dal turns brown; it burns within seconds.
Add the onions and fry until browned. Add the turmeric and sauté for 2 minutes, then the ginger and garlic for a few seconds.
Add the potatoes and mix well. Turn off the heat, add the lemon juice and coriander leaves, and mix again.
Heat a tava or frying pan over medium heat until a drop of water evaporates on contact.
Pour on about 1/2 cup batter and spread it slowly outwards into a thin, round dosa.
Cook for a minute, then flip it. As the other side cooks, spread some of the ghee and shortening mixture on top.
Flip it again. As the bottom crisps, spread 1 tsp of the onion chutney evenly over the top.
Spoon some potato filling onto one half, fold the other half over and serve with the coconut chutney.

recipes.title: Dum ka Keema (Smoked Mince)
recipes.description: Minced meat marinated with fried onion paste, ginger and yogurt, smoked with charcoal, then slow-cooked.

steps.instructionText: Heat the oil in a heavy saucepan. Fry the onions, stirring often, for 8-10 minutes until light golden.
Lift out the onions, then fry the whole red chillies in the same oil for just a moment so they don't burn.
Keep the oil aside. Blend the onions and red chillies to a smooth paste without any water.
Wash the mince well and squeeze out the water.
Put the mince in a bowl with the onion paste, ginger paste, salt, garam masala and yogurt. Knead well with your hands until smooth.
Cover and marinate at room temperature for 3-4 hours, or overnight in the fridge; mix in the papaya paste for the last hour.
Heat the charcoal over a medium flame until it is red hot and covered in white ash.
Spread the mince in a metal pan with a well in the centre. Put a piece of foil in the well, set the hot charcoal on it and add 2-3 drops of oil.
Cover tightly at once and set aside to smoke for 20-25 minutes.
Discard the charcoal. Heat 1/2 cup of the reserved oil in a heavy pan and fry the mince over low heat for 4-5 minutes.
Cover tightly and cook for 15-20 minutes, until all the moisture is absorbed.
Serve garnished with the green chillies and coriander leaves.

recipes.title: Garam Masala
recipes.description: Homemade North Indian garam masala of toasted whole spices, mace and rose petals, ground to a fine powder.

steps.instructionText: Toast the bay leaves, black and green cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, coriander, cumin, fennel, mace, peppercorns and rose petals one at a time in a dry pan.
Keep the heat low and shake the pan until each spice is a shade darker and aromatic; take care not to burn them.
Transfer the toasted spices to a cool container and let them cool.
Grind all the spices together with the ginger powder to an even powder in a grinder or mortar.

recipes.title: Hyderabadi Haleem
recipes.description: Slow-cooked paste of whole wheat and mutton with green chillies, ginger and garlic, topped with fried onions.

steps.instructionText: Remove any bran from the wheat, wash it and soak for 2 hours.
Grind the ginger, garlic, green chillies and salt to a paste. Rub it over the mutton and marinate for 1 hour.
Pressure cook the soaked wheat and the marinated mutton for about 45 minutes.
Mince the cooked wheat and mutton, then grind them to a fine paste.
Heat the oil in a pan and fry the onions until brown. Lift out a few for garnish, then add the turmeric and garam masala.
Add the ground paste and cook over low heat, stirring occasionally, until it comes away from the sides of the pan.
Adjust the salt and serve hot, garnished with lime wedges, coriander leaves and the fried onions.

recipes.title: Pakistani Chai
recipes.description: Strong cardamom tea made by adding hot milk to boiling tea leaves and taking it to the brink of boiling over.

steps.instructionText: Bring the water to a simmer in a saucepan over medium-high heat. Tear open the cardamom pods and add them.
Heat the milk in the microwave for 2 minutes, until it is close to boiling.
When the water nearly boils, slowly add the tea leaves.
Add the hot milk until the tea turns light brown, then raise the heat to high. Stir continuously if you added too much milk.
Take the pan off the heat just as the chai is about to boil over, and strain it into cups.
Sweeten with sugar if you like.

recipes.title: Karnataka Rasam
recipes.description: Karnataka-style rasam of toor dal and tomatoes (or tamarind) with coconut and a mustard-cumin tempering.

steps.instructionText: Pressure cook the toor dal with enough water until soft.
If using tomatoes, parboil them, remove the skins and chop roughly.
Add the salt, chilli powder, turmeric powder and the tomatoes (or tamarind paste) to the cooked dal. Simmer for 3-4 minutes.
Add the hing, grated coconut and coriander powder. Simmer for a few more minutes to cook the coconut.
Heat the oil in a small frying pan over medium heat and add the mustard seeds and cumin seeds.
When the mustard seeds pop, take the pan off the heat and pour the tempering into the rasam with the curry leaves.
Garnish with the coriander leaves and serve.

recipes.title: Khaman Dhokla
recipes.description: Soft, spongy Gujarati steamed besan cake topped with a mustard seed, sesame and green chilli tempering.

steps.instructionText: Grease a 12 cm (5-inch) round tin with 1/2 tsp of the oil.
Mix the besan, semolina, sugar, ginger-chilli paste and salt with just enough water to make a thick batter.
Add the fruit salt and 2 tsp water. When bubbles form, mix gently to spread it through the batter.
Pour the batter into the tin straight away and swirl the tin to spread it evenly.
Put the tin in a steamer at once, cover and steam for 12-15 minutes, until the dhokla is cooked. Let it cool slightly.
Heat the remaining oil in a small pan and add the mustard seeds.
When they crackle, add the sesame seeds, green chillies, curry leaves and hing. Sauté over a medium flame for a few minutes, stirring.
Take the tempering off the heat and stir in 2 tbsp water.
Unmould the dhokla and cut it into equal pieces. Spoon the tempering over, garnish with the coriander leaves and serve at once.

recipes.title: Langar Dal
recipes.description: Simple gurdwara-style dal pressure cooked with onion, turmeric and ghee.

steps.instructionText: Rinse the dal three times and drain off the water.
Chop the onion into small cubes about 1 cm across.
Melt the ghee in a pressure cooker with the lid off.
Add the onion and sauté for 3 minutes.
Add the turmeric powder and mix it well with the onion and ghee.
Add the dal, water and salt. Close the lid and seal the valve.
Pressure cook for 12 minutes.
Let the pressure release naturally, then serve the dal.

recipes.title: Kerala Meat Masala
recipes.description: Kerala spice mix of toasted chillies, coriander and pepper, used as a rub or paste for mutton.

steps.instructionText: Toast the dried red chillies, coriander seeds, peppercorns, cumin seeds and mustard seeds in a frying pan.
Grind them with the turmeric powder, cloves, cardamom seeds and cinnamon to a powder.
Store the masala in a glass jar with a tight-fitting lid.
To use, rub it on meat as a dry powder or mixed with oil into a paste, and marinate for 20 minutes to 2 hours before cooking.

recipes.title: Pulikachal (Tamarind Rice Mix)
recipes.description: Tamil spiced tamarind paste, cooked down with dals and roasted spices, for mixing into rice as puliyodharai.

steps.instructionText: Dry roast the coriander seeds, fenugreek seeds and sesame seeds without oil, then grind them to a fine powder.
Heat the oil in a pan and fry the urad dal, chana dal, red chillies and peanuts, if using, for a few minutes.
Add the tamarind extract and salt and bring to a boil.
Add the ground spice powder and the hing and mix well.
Stir constantly until the paste is thick, the oil floats on top and it no longer sticks to the pan.
Cool and refrigerate. To serve, mix the pulikachal with cooked rice.

recipes.title: Watalappam
recipes.description: Sri Lankan steamed custard of coconut milk, jaggery and eggs, spiced with cardamom and cloves.

steps.instructionText: Beat the eggs in a mixer.
Add the coconut milk, jaggery, cardamom powder and cloves to the eggs and mix well.
Pour the mixture into a heatproof pot and steam for 20 minutes.
Top the watalappam with the cashews.

recipes.title: Spicy Chickpea Soup
recipes.description: Quick blender soup of chickpeas, coconut milk, salsa and garam masala, simmered for a few minutes.

steps.instructionText: Purée the chickpeas, coconut milk, chicken broth, salsa, garam masala, ginger, apple juice concentrate and coriander leaves in a blender until smooth.
Pour into a large saucepan and bring to a simmer.
Simmer for 4-5 minutes, stirring often, to blend the flavours.

recipes.title: Besan Omelette
recipes.description: Eggless omelette of besan batter with turmeric and paprika, cooked in olive oil until set.

steps.instructionText: Mix the besan, baking powder, salt, turmeric and paprika in a bowl.
Gradually add the soy milk and mix until the batter is smooth.
Heat a skillet over medium heat, add the olive oil and spread it across the pan.
Pour in the batter and cook until bubbles form in the middle, then carefully flip it with a spatula.
Cook the other side for about 30 seconds, then serve.

recipes.title: Doubles (Trinidad Bara & Chana)
recipes.description: Trinidad street snack: fried turmeric bara sandwiching curried chickpeas, with pepper sauce and chutney.

steps.instructionText: In a large bowl, mix the flour, 1/2 tsp of the salt, the turmeric powder, 1/2 tsp cumin, the sugar and the yeast.
Add enough lukewarm water to make a soft dough. Mix well, cover and let it rise for 2 hours.
Boil the soaked chickpeas in salted water until tender, then drain well.
Heat the vegetable oil in a heavy skillet. Add the garlic, onion and the curry powder mixed with 1/4 cup of the water, and sauté for a few minutes.
Add the chickpeas, stir to coat and cook for 5 minutes. Add 1 cup water, a pinch of cumin, 1 tsp salt and some pepper.
Cover, lower the heat and simmer until the chickpeas are soft and moist, adding water if needed. Adjust the seasoning.
Punch down the dough and let it relax for 15 minutes.
For each bara, pat about 1 tbsp of dough into a 10-12 cm circle, wetting your palms with water.
Fry a few baras at a time in the hot oil, turning once, and drain on kitchen paper.
Sandwich 2 tbsp of the chickpeas between 2 baras. Add hot pepper sauce and mango chutney to taste.
